title: GST 115 ( UNIZIK ) : INTRODUCTION TO READING AND READING SKILLS
subject: GST 115

questions.question: Which position does reading occupy among the four main language skills?
questions.explanation: Reading is the third of the four main language skills alongside listening, speaking, and writing.

questions.question: Reading critically in education primarily helps students to achieve which outcome?
questions.explanation: Reading critically helps one make good choices, evaluate what to read, and understand key points.

questions.question: Which description matches reading as a cognitive process?
questions.explanation: Reading is defined as a cognitive process that involves decoding symbols to arrive at meaning.

questions.question: Reading is classified as which type of language skill?
questions.explanation: Reading is a receptive skill that allows us to receive information.

questions.question: The process of looking at a series of written symbols to get meaning is known as which activity?
questions.explanation: Reading is the process of looking at a series of written symbols and getting meaning from them.

questions.question: Which term describes perceiving a written text silently to understand its contents?
questions.explanation: Perceiving a written text to understand its contents can be done silently as silent reading.

questions.question: When a written text is read aloud, it is referred to as which type of reading?
questions.explanation: When we say a written text aloud, it is called oral reading.

questions.question: Reading words accurately requires the integration of visual, auditory, and which other type of skills?
questions.explanation: Reading words accurately requires the integration of visual, auditory, and cognitive skills.

questions.question: Reading provides access to stories from around the world which helps people to become more of which trait?
questions.explanation: Reading stories helps to understand people and make them more empathetic.

questions.question: Boosting knowledge and brainpower is achieved through which activity?
questions.explanation: Reading improves memory, boosts knowledge and brainpower.

questions.question: Identifying the words we see during reading is known as which process?
questions.explanation: To be able to read, we need to identify the words we see which is word recognition.

questions.question: Understanding the meaning of the words we read is called which process?
questions.explanation: To be able to read, we need to understand what words mean which is comprehension.

questions.question: Connecting words and their meaning so that reading becomes automatic is termed which ability?
questions.explanation: Connecting words and their meaning so reading is automatic is fluency.

questions.question: Reading improves focus, concentration, and increases which personal trait?
questions.explanation: Reading improves focus and concentration and increases imagination and creativity.

questions.question: Learning to read consists of developing skills in reading accurately and which other critical area?
questions.explanation: The Simple View of Reading includes reading words accurately/fluently and comprehending the meaning.

questions.question: Recognizing words automatically and pronouncing them quickly is known as which skill?
questions.explanation: Fluency improves as students recognize words automatically and pronounce them quickly.

questions.question: Reading the word dig instead of dog hinders comprehension due to a lack of which skill?
questions.explanation: Reading words inaccurately like dig for dog hinders comprehension.

questions.question: Seeing each letter in a word accurately requires which type of acuity?
questions.explanation: Seeing each letter accurately in print requires visual acuity.

questions.question: Producing the sound each letter makes relies on which type of perception?
questions.explanation: Producing the sound each letter makes requires auditory perception.

questions.question: Understanding an example sentence about dogs and cats requires which element?
questions.explanation: Background knowledge assists comprehension of sentences about dogs and cats.

questions.question: Background knowledge assists comprehension by helping students understand concepts like size and which other feature?
questions.explanation: Students must know what bark means and that little and big refer to size concepts.

questions.question: A student sensing the irony of a little dog barking at a big cat demonstrates which deeper understanding?
questions.explanation: Understanding the irony in a sentence shows text comprehension.

questions.question: Browsing through reading material to look for main ideas is a technique known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Skimming is a speed-reading technique where the reader browses for main ideas.

questions.question: Skimming is compared to lifting which part of milk?
questions.explanation: Skimming is like lifting the cream off the top of the milk.

questions.question: Sourcing relevant information quickly and saving time are advantages of which reading technique?
questions.explanation: Advantages of skimming include sourcing relevant information quickly and saving time.

questions.question: Searching for a specific piece of information within a text is called which skill?
questions.explanation: Scanning enables the reader to look for a specific piece of information.

questions.question: Scanning is also known by which alternative term?
questions.explanation: Scanning is called search-reading.

questions.question: Looking for a particular number in a phone directory is an example of which technique?
questions.explanation: A reader can scan for a particular number in a phone directory.

questions.question: The reading process that ends as soon as the required information is reached is which technique?
questions.explanation: In scanning, the search ends as soon as the information is reached.

questions.question: Reading texts for enjoyment or leisure is categorized as which type of reading?
questions.explanation: Extensive reading involves learners reading texts for enjoyment or leisure.

questions.question: An approach that encourages students to read a large number of easy books is known as which reading?
questions.explanation: Extensive Reading encourages students to read many relatively easy books.

questions.question: Extensive reading enhances general language competence and develops which other asset?
questions.explanation: Extensive reading helps develop general knowledge.

questions.question: Extensive reading consolidates and sustains growth in which area?
questions.explanation: Extensive reading extends, consolidates, and sustains vocabulary growth.

questions.question: Reading widely during extensive reading increases one's reading speed and which other metric?
questions.explanation: Extensive reading increases the amount of material one reads and reading speed.

questions.question: Creating pleasure and relaxation is a benefit associated with which reading type?
questions.explanation: Extensive reading creates pleasure and relaxation.

questions.question: Detailed reading to understand the text and learn language features is called which technique?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading involves detailed reading with the goals of understanding text and learning language features.

questions.question: Intensive reading is typically applied to texts that learners would find what without help?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading texts are typically ones learners would have difficulty reading unassisted.

questions.question: Developing critical thinking and improving analytical skills is a goal of which reading approach?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading aims to develop critical thinking and analytical skills.

questions.question: Intensive reading is a great tool for improving fluency and which other reading metric?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading is a great tool for improving fluency and reading speed.

questions.question: Understanding an author's intentions is a key goal of which reading technique?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading aims to understand subject matter and the author's intentions.

questions.question: Learning new skills like making inferences and identifying main ideas occurs in which reading type?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading involves learning new skills such as making inferences.

questions.question: Analyzing, interpreting, and sometimes evaluating a text is a process known as which reading?
questions.explanation: Critical reading is a process of analyzing, interpreting, and sometimes evaluating.

questions.question: Questioning both the text and our own reading is a feature of which reading approach?
questions.explanation: When we read critically, we question both the text and our own reading of it.

questions.question: Judging whether an author is biased or truthful is a primary focus of which reading?
questions.explanation: Critical reading judges the writer in terms of truthfulness, bias, and knowledge.

questions.question: Critical reading requires full concentration and makes the reader a perfect which of the following?
questions.explanation: Critical reading involves full concentration and makes the reader a perfect intellectual.

questions.question: Leading to innovation, invention, or propounding a theory is a result of which reading?
questions.explanation: Critical reading leads to innovation, invention, or propounding a theory or principle.

questions.question: Reading involves a complex integration of skills and serves as which type of skill?
questions.explanation: Reading is a receptive skill through which information is received.

questions.question: Proficient readers make reading look effortless, but reading instruction requires which approach?
questions.explanation: Reading instruction for all students requires systematic instruction in word reading and comprehension.

questions.question: Developing appropriate reading skills helps minimize the waste of which two elements?
questions.explanation: Developing appropriate reading skills minimizes waste of time and energy.

questions.question: For students who struggle with reading, instruction and intervention must be carefully planned to address which issues?
questions.explanation: Problem areas must be determined, and instruction and intervention must be carefully planned to address them.
